_provenance: Every label below is Adam Khoo's OWN verdict extracted verbatim from docs/VMI_MASTER_DOCUMENT.md (line refs given). No analyst consensus, no Morningstar ratings, no third-party moat data. These are the gold anchors for training.
_grading_scale: verdict: wide | narrow | none | wide_weak (passes but Adam concedes weak spots) | none_or_narrow (avoided, disruptable) | lost_moat (had one, decayed). score10 given only where Adam stated it. source_scores per the 5 sources only where the doc gives a per-source breakdown.
_scoring_rule: "If a company has got at least THREE out of these FIVE moat sources, then I would want to invest in the company." (doc line ~4396)
key_man_rule: "once you lose the talent, the whole business is gone" — key-man dependence is a moat weakness. Validates avoiding businesses whose value collapses if one person leaves.

labels.adam_reasoning: Largest global social media and digital advertising ecosystem (Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Messenger, Threads). ~3.5B of ~6B internet users use a Meta product (~60%). No competitor (Twitter/X, Snapchat, Reddit) comes close. Network effect 10/10.

Growing well during the pandemic, 'but I felt that although Zoom was growing, it didn't have a very strong moat. It could easily be disrupted by bigger competitors like Microsoft and Google.' Barriers 5/10: bigger competitors can always replicate a similar platform. Switching 6/10: you can easily switch to another platform. NOT BOUGHT — 'I don't often invest in 6 out of 10.'
No pricing power, no brand loyalty, no barriers to entry, no switching costs, no network effect, low economies of scale. 'No moat is the most dangerous.' AVOIDED; subsequently collapsed.

'Although PayPal was gaining traction, it was getting popular, it was growing, but I felt that the business itself could be easily disrupted and replaced by much stronger competitors. And good thing I didn't buy it, because after going up initially, these shares have collapsed and I still wouldn't buy it.'

Near-perfect across all five sources; network effect and barriers to entry both 10/10. Brand monopoly: 'we say Google this, Google that, not Bing this.' YouTube = top-of-mind free video. Search/Gemini flywheel: more usage → smarter searches → more powerful AI. Weak spot conceded: Google Cloud a 'distant third' behind AWS and Azure.

Clean pass — THREE of the five sources demonstrated: brand monopoly (top-of-mind office software), switching costs, network effect. Barriers to entry and economies of scale not separately argued. Long-run chart 'always goes up.'

'At least two or three' sources. Brand monopoly YES (e-commerce + cloud top-of-mind). Barriers YES (Prime same-day delivery — scale lets them do it faster/cheaper than anyone). Scale YES ('you bet'). Network effect 'maybe not' — explicitly declined. Switching costs SPLIT BY SEGMENT: NO for individual e-commerce shoppers (can buy on Alibaba tomorrow, eBay next day), YES for AWS enterprise (expensive and difficult to migrate to Azure). AWS 33% cloud share Q2 2020, clear leader. Weakest of the three big-tech verdicts.

Pricing-power test FAILED: cannot raise car prices annually without losing share; heavy EV competition from China; 'not only can they not raise their price, they have to keep cutting their price, they have to keep discounting.' → narrow moat, not wide. Also in a structurally no-moat industry (auto manufacturers).
